papers.title_in_file: A scalable advantage in multi-photon quantum machine learning
papers.partial_detail: Main text read in full; Supplementary Notes are not in the file.
papers.what_it_is: Theory and photonic-chip experiments on how learning capacity of linear optical circuits scales with photon number, tested on unitary learning and metric learning.

assertions.value: The paper proves that the learning capacity of linear optical circuits scales polynomially with the photon number.
assertions.anchor: Results, Eq. 6, p.3-4; proof in Supplementary Note 2.2 (not in file)
quotes: we prove that the learning capacity of linear optical circuits scales polynomially with the photon number
A complete proof is provided in Supplementary Note 2.2.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as proved in the paper; proof is in Supplementary Note 2.2, which the file does not contain.

assertions.value: The authors report that in an experiment on a photonic chip, two-photon states generalized with L = 2 training states, while single-photon states needed L = 4 and L = 3 was insufficient.
quotes: In contrast, two-photon states generalize successfully with only L = 2, requiring half as much training data as the single-photon case.
training states (L = 4) are required, while three (L = 3) are insufficient
assertions.certainty_reason: One experimental study on one small unitary task.
assertions.reader_inference: The training-set size where generalization occurs was measured for one unitary size only.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the metric-learning experiment, both average accuracy and class separation improve markedly for n = 2 compared to n = 1.
quotes: for n = 2, both the average accuracy and class separation improve markedly compared to n = 1
assertions.certainty_reason: Single experiment on one vowel dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state they restrict the study to Fock states with at most one photon per mode, and that the framework currently targets product states as input.
quotes: Here, we restrict ourselves to Fock states with at most one photon per mode
while our framework currently targets product states as input
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope and limit.

papers.title_in_file: Efficient Quantum Algorithm for Robust Training
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Results (informal theorem), Discussion, and the readout-assumption paragraph after Theorem 1; appendix proofs not read.
papers.what_it_is: A theoretical reduction of projected-gradient adversarial training to a sparse linear system solved by a quantum linear-system routine, with a query-complexity theorem.

assertions.value: The authors state that the dominant query cost scales linearly with training time steps, up to logarithmic factors, and polylogarithmically with model size, under local stability and sparsity assumptions.
quotes: Here we give an end-to-end quantum procedure for projected-gradient robust training under local stability and sparsity assumptions.
the dominant query cost scales linearly with training time steps, up to logarithmic factors, and polylogarithmically with model size
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 (stated in Methods) with proofs in the Appendix; result holds only under the stated assumptions.

assertions.value: The paper states that the theorem assumes oracle access to the system matrix, a preparation routine for the right-hand side, and readout assumptions on the terminal parameter block.
quotes: under explicit terminal-weight and sparse-output readout assumptions
The theorem further assumes oracle access to the rescaled system matrix together with a preparation routine for the right-hand side
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the access and readout assumptions its theorem relies on.

assertions.value: The authors state that three technical directions remain and that extending the reduction to broader robust-training architectures and to transport-based threat models remains open.
quotes: Three technical directions remain.
Extending the reduction to broader robust-training architectures and to transport-based threat models remains open
assertions.certainty_reason: The Discussion states the open directions.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, Results and Analysis opening, Discussion and Outlook; Sections 3-5 and appendices only skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: Introduces quantum models whose data-encoding generator is built from each input matrix, and compares them with rotation-gate encoders on Pendigits and two synthetic tasks.

assertions.value: The authors report that at the largest evaluated circuit depth the Quantum Spectral Model variants lead the tested quantum models in mean test accuracy across all four benchmarks.
quotes: At the largest evaluated circuit depth, QSM variants lead the tested quantum models in mean test accuracy across all four benchmarks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on four small benchmarks.
assertions.reader_inference: The lead is over the quantum comparison models only; the Discussion says classical baselines that lead on the present benchmarks would be retained in later comparisons.

assertions.value: The authors report a task-dependent reversal in ablations: subspace-preserving controls perform better on Pendigits, while spectral-value-only controls lead among the tested ablations on the synthetic tasks.
quotes: Ablations show a task-dependent reversal: subspace-preserving controls perform better on Pendigits, whereas spectral-valueonly controls lead among the tested ablations on the synthetic tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical ablation from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the specific contribution of locality remains unresolved and that future work should test how broadly the observed representation effects persist across model scales, datasets and resource constraints.
quotes: the specific contribution of locality remains unresolved
future work can test how broadly the observed representation effects persist across model scales, datasets and resource constraints
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limits.

papers.title_in_file: A Review of Variational Quantum Algorithms: Insights into Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section on challenges (barren plateaus), QML application opening, and conclusion; remaining survey sections not read.
papers.what_it_is: A review of variational quantum algorithms from the NISQ era toward early fault-tolerant and fault-tolerant regimes.

assertions.value: The review reports, citing other work, that barren plateaus make gradients vanish exponentially with system size, rendering the optimization landscape effectively flat for any polynomial number of samples.
quotes: A central barrier to trainability is the BPs phenomenon, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, rendering the optimization landscape effectively flat for any polynomial number of samples
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to cited work.

assertions.value: The authors state that variational quantum algorithms may enter a renewed phase of relevance rather than become obsolete with fault-tolerant computers, provided their frameworks are systematically adapted.
quotes: Rather than being rendered obsolete by the emergence of fault-tolerant quantum computers, VQAs may enter a renewed phase of relevance, provided that their frameworks are systematically adapted for this new computational landscape.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author view in a review, with no new evidence.

assertions.value: The review states, citing other work, that Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks are a critical direction due to their immunity to barren plateaus.
quotes: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks represent a critical direction due to their immunity to BPs
assertions.certainty_reason: Statement attributed to cited work.

papers.title_in_file: XGSwap: eXtreme Gradient boosting Swap for Routing in NISQ Devices
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, training and validation, results, discussion and conclusion; background and method sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A gradient-boosting model that predicts CNOT-path fidelity on a 127-qubit IBM device to choose routing paths, tested on random CNOT gates.

assertions.value: The authors report that on hardware the XGSwap path differed from the shortest path in 138 out of 313 experiments and gave higher fidelity in 76 out of 138 of those.
quotes: We observe that the path identified by XGSwap is different from the shortest path in 138 out of 313 experiments.
In 76 out of 138 experiments, the path identified by XGSwap yields higher fidelity than the shortest path.
assertions.certainty_reason: One device, one short hardware run.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract cites more than 200 tests and the results section cites more than 300 runs; the counts are not stated consistently.

assertions.value: The authors state the model predicts the best path for a single CNOT gate and does not consider the overall circuit, and was trained on a single quantum processor so its performance elsewhere can only be speculated.
quotes: our model solely predicts the best path for a given CNOT gate, and does not consider the overall circuit
the model was trained on a single quantum processor, and we can only speculate on its performance on other devices
assertions.certainty_reason: The conclusion states the limits.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum information processing with superconducting circuits: a perspective
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section 4.4 on useful NISQ advantage, and section 5.5 final perspective; applications and hardware sections not read in detail.
papers.what_it_is: A perspective review of superconducting-qubit quantum computing, benchmarks, variational algorithms and routes to practical quantum advantage.

assertions.value: The author states that useful NISQ digital quantum advantage is probably mission impossible in the NISQ era.
quotes: The short answer is: yes, unfortunately probably mission impossible in the NISQ era.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author judgement in a perspective article.

assertions.value: The author states that it is currently impossible to build superconducting processors where one can entangle more than about 20 qubits with high probability during the coherence time.
quotes: it is currently impossible to build superconducting quantum processing units (QPU) where one can entangle more than about 20 qubits with high probability during the coherence time
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement of field status as of February 2023, no single study behind it.

assertions.value: The author reports, citing Goings et al., that a large classically intractable CYP model simulation may need 5 million qubits and nearly 10 billion Toffoli gates, and may take 100 QPU hours.
quotes: a large classically intractable CYP model simulation may need 5 million qubits and nearly 10 billion Toffoli gates, and may take 100 QPU hours
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to cited work.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results and discussion text, summary and limitations; derivations not read in detail.
papers.what_it_is: A framework that encodes topological information of simplicial complexes into quantum states through Laplacian-driven evolution, tested on classical simulation of clique-complex classification.

assertions.value: The authors report that the quantum representations consistently outperform a baseline based on direct comparisons of the combinatorial Laplacians, and describe the evidence as preliminary.
quotes: provide preliminary evidence that topology-driven quantum representations can capture discriminative information beyond that available through direct comparisons of classical topological descriptors
The proposed quantum representations consistently outperform a baseline based on direct comparisons of the combinatorial Laplacians describing the underlying topological structure.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study run in classical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state the empirical evaluation was restricted to a finite collection of benchmark datasets and relatively small problem instances compatible with classical simulation.
quotes: our empirical evaluation was restricted to a finite collection of benchmark datasets and relatively small problem instances that are compatible with classical simulation of quantum systems
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit.

assertions.value: The authors state they do not provide formal guarantees regarding quantum advantage, expressive power, or generalisation performance, and that the origin of the advantage is not fully understood.
quotes: we do not provide formal guarantees regarding quantum advantage, expressive power, or generalisation performance
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit.
